articles.title: Indian jewellery body alerts BIS over suspected gold adulteration, urges jewellers to tighten quality checks
articles.excerpt:
The All India Gem and Jewellery Domestic Council (GJC) has alerted the Bureau of Indian Standards (BIS) over reports of suspected use of Rhenium- and Iridium-based alloys to increase the weight of gold jewellery without a corresponding increase in purity, urging jewellers and consumers to remain vigilant.

The industry body said BIS was taking the matter seriously and maintaining close vigilance. However, it cautioned against panic, saying isolated reports should not undermine consumer confidence in the Indian gems and jewellery industry.

Rajesh Rokde, Chairman, GJC, said jewellers must undertake stringent quality control checks on gold procured from manufacturers, wholesalers and suppliers

articles.excerpt:
The Indian rupee has strengthened past the 93-per-dollar mark for the first time since April. This recovery is attributed to over $12 billion of foreign investments in Indian equities in November. Hedge funds have unwound bearish positions on the rupee, contributing to its recent gains. The Reserve Bank of India has taken measures to support the local currency amidst stabilization efforts.
